one_line: Our accessible restroom/shower trailers and fitness facilities match part of this, but the shoot house, site work, and $20M–$50M size are far beyond our largest past contract ($408,482), so track it and go after a subcontract or team role instead of bidding as prime.
scope: The Secret Service wants turnkey temporary facilities at the James J. Rowley Training Center in Laurel, MD. The contractor would furnish, install, maintain, and remove three things: a climate-controlled temporary fitness facility for strength, cardio, and functional conditioning; a temporary shoot house next to it; and accessible restroom and shower trailers. The contractor also handles site preparation, utilities, power generation and distribution, lighting, life-safety systems, equipment options, and site restoration after removal, all to Government-approved plans.
fit: Accessible restroom and shower trailers are a core product. The proposal template lists ADA units on request, sealed gray/black tanks, independent HVAC, and on-demand hot water.
Our fleet list includes Recreation and Fitness Facilities, which matches the climate-controlled temporary fitness facility.
Facility Support & Utilities is a core competency: generators, water delivery, waste removal, and portable sanitation. That covers part of the power generation and utilities scope.
We have turnkey DHS past performance: USCG Station Lake Worth Inlet (70Z02826FMIAM0008, $78,500), which covered berthing, restroom/shower trailers, water/wastewater, maintenance, and demobilization.
We have turnkey basecamp experience at federal sites: Fort Lee, VA ($408,482, as a sub), Camp Lejeune ($239,760), and Portsmouth Naval Shipyard (~$130,000).
Our operations cover the full install-to-removal cycle: deployment in 24–72 hours, weekly servicing, 24/7 emergency line, weekly QC reports to the COR, and a personnel access roster.
No set-aside is stated, so not holding 8(a), WOSB, SDVOSB, or HUBZone status doesn't block us. SAM is active. Our work area is nationwide, which covers Laurel, MD.
red_flags: This is a HigherGov contract forecast (source URL /contract-forecast/10000572), not a released solicitation. The pack has 0 attachments: no SOW, no instructions, no evaluation criteria.

Estimated value is $20M–$50M. Our largest listed contract is $408,482 (Fort Lee, as a sub), so this is roughly 50–120 times our largest past job. That is a serious risk for prime-level past performance and financial capacity.
The temporary shoot house is outside every core competency and fleet item in our profile.
Site preparation, power distribution, life-safety systems, and work to Government-approved plans point to engineering or construction-type work our profile doesn't list.
NAICS 532289 and PSC R429 are not among our listed NAICS codes (721310, 532490, 722310, 624230, 624221, 561210, 423740; 532120 per the template) or PSC codes (W023, W099, W045).
Unrestricted competition (no set-aside stated) for a $20M–$50M requirement will probably draw large, established firms.
The price list has no prices for either ADA shower-restroom combination row (3 Stalls + 1 ADA; 8 Stalls + 1 ADA), and this requirement specifically calls for accessible units.
The profile shows no bonding capacity, construction licenses, or Maryland licenses, and a requirement this size may call for them.
The response date (2027-01-29) is a forecast date with no time or time zone and may change.
competition: This is listed as a new requirement, and the pack names no incumbent. This agency's past NAICS 532289 awards were small rentals: tents, furniture, golf carts, and dignitary-visit support. They ran from $4,515 (Grimes Events & Party Tents) to $329,778 (DJ Doctor, Tents and Generators, Bedminster NJ, 14 offers). Other awardees were Cort Business Services ($72,430, 1 offer), Checkmate Global (3 awards, $4,765–$81,008), IN Tents Party Rentals ($89,776), Jads Productions ($46,715), Ranco Tent Rental ($17,116), Maddox Joines ($87,167), and Horizon Distributors ($78,300). Most drew 1–3 offers. In the any-agency benchmarks, Asset Group won 7 FEMA mobile DRC call orders ($276,806–$2,047,173, 3–5 offers) and Rapid Deployment won $6,954,827 (5 offers). None of them won anything near this size, and none of these awards had a shoot-house or fitness-facility scope.
price_signal: The forecast estimates $20M–$50M. No similar award in the pack comes close. The largest NAICS 532289 + PSC R429 benchmark is $6,954,827 (Rapid Deployment, FEMA), and this agency's largest 532289 award is $329,778. For our share of the work: the USCG template prices restroom/shower trailer rental at $8,995/unit for a 30-day job (quoted total $51,990; related award $78,500). The price list shows Luxury Shower-Restroom Combination Trailers at 3,995–5,995 for 15 days–1 month and 2,495–5,995 for more than 3 months, with no billing basis stated. The ADA rows have no prices.
